messages.text:
"Create an ultra-detailed, hyper-immersive, expansive, long-form, and production-ready 3D 8-bit pixel-art survival horror and laboratory escape game titled \"Ape Project\". The entire game world—spanning a secure 15x15m laboratory lobby with interactive hydraulic doors, a massive 500x500m slightly hilly sparse jungle exterior, a Lethal-Ape-inspired player character, and the terrifying blind auditory predator \"Mossman\"—must be rendered strictly through high-end 3D 8-bit pixel-art engines combined with dynamic voxel-grid physics and moody lighting shaders, completely avoiding flat 2D sprites or high-poly realistic models. All visual assets, hydraulic animations, particle trails, and creature AI behaviors are dynamically generated in real-time.
1. Laboratory Lobby @COMMENT_BODY@ Hydraulic Door Architecture (15x15M)
The Starting Zone: Upon launching a new game, the player spawns inside a secure, high-tech subterranean laboratory lobby measuring precisely 15x15 meters.
Interior Elements: The room is lined with detailed 3D 8-bit pixel-art laboratory racks and storage shelves filled with scientific equipment and chemical containers.
4-Way Hydraulic Door System: Heavy hydraulic security doors are located at the left, right, front, and back walls of the laboratory.
Interactive Door Controls: Each door features an interactive control switch positioned precisely on the left side of the door frame. Players can manually press this switch to trigger the smooth hydraulic open/close cycle to control exits and entries.
2. Exterior Open-World Jungle Map (500x500M)
The Wilderness: Stepping outside the laboratory leads directly into an expansive, open-world jungle map measuring 500x500 meters.
Terrain @COMMENT_BODY@ Foliage: The landscape features rolling, slightly hilly terrain interspersed with sparse, scattered 3D pixel-art trees, providing open lines of sight mixed with tactical cover points.
3. Player Model @COMMENT_BODY@ Animation (Lethal Ape Style)
Player Character: A highly detailed 3D 8-bit pixel-art ape character model directly inspired by the iconic style of Lethal Ape, featuring rugged textures, fluid retro locomotion cycles, climbing frames, and responsive movement controls.
4. Monster Ecosystem: Mossman
The primary threat roaming the 500x500m outdoor jungle, hunting purely by sound:
Monster Designation: Mossman
Spawn Zone: Deployed across the outdoor jungle map.
Physical Morphology @COMMENT_BODY@ Appearance:
Height: Towering at 2.8 meters.
Color @COMMENT_BODY@ Texture: Bright moss-green base skin covered with dark green moss stripes winding across and around its entire body.
Facial Features: Completely eyeless (no eyes whatsoever), with only a wide, unsettlingly visible mouth showing on its face.
Combat @COMMENT_BODY@ Movement Statistics:
Movement Speed: Blistering fast at 33 KM/h.
Turning Agility/Difficulty: 50% turning resistance (momentum-based turning inertia that requires wide arcs when changing directions at top speed).
Sensory System @COMMENT_BODY@ Abilities:
Sensory Traits: Blind (cannot see the player), but equipped with Super Sensitive Hearing (tracks footsteps, door activations, and sound ripples across the map).
Unique Ability: Continuously emits glowing green particle effects from its body and footsteps as it walks through the jungle.
5. Visual Art Direction @COMMENT_BODY@ Retro 8-Bit Polish
3D Pixel-Art Fidelity: Crisp, hand-crafted 3D 8-bit pixel textures mapped onto low-poly meshes, featuring high-contrast retro color palettes, atmospheric fog over the hilly terrain, and dynamic shadow casting.
Audio-Visual Immersion: Eerie ambient jungle soundscapes, heavy hydraulic mechanical clanks, and sharp audio cues that trigger the Mossman's super-sensitive hearing if the player moves too loudly outside the lab. (3D Game, Phone/Tablet)

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"
